references.text: Earlier in the same chapter God promises to remove wild animals from the land as a blessing; here he threatens to send them as a curse.
Moses' song describes the teeth of wild animals as part of God's judgment on an disobedient people.
Lions were sent among the foreign peoples who settled in Samaria because they did not fear the Lord.
Isaiah prophesies about desolate places where wild animals will dwell as a sign of God's judgment.
Describes how roads become empty and abandoned as a consequence of forsaking God's way.
Jeremiah mentions wild animals as one of four instruments of punishment the Lord sends against his people.
Ezekiel describes wild animals as one of four severe judgments God sends over a land.
Ezekiel lists the four judgments: sword, famine, wild animals, and pestilence.
Hosea describes how God will attack like a wild animal and tear them apart.
Revelation mentions the wild beasts of the earth as one of four instruments of punishment, echoing Old Testament prophecies.
